the onset and propagation (in the case of a single fibre) of a fibre-matric interface crack in a composite subjected to remote biaxially-transverse loads.

the present interface model provides a simple, robust and efficient tool for studying the onset and propagation (including mixed-mode) of an interface failure under proportional biaxial loads.

this new interface model is able to capture the onset of debonding at the interface, and to predict the debond onset load and location.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the considered interface model, the onset of a debond at the interface is not necessarily associated with the formation of a crack tip in the matrix.
, for the considered configurations, the interface debond onset and propagation can occur in a region of the interface where the interface fracture toughness is not minimum.

the interface model presented here, in spite of its simplicity, can be applied for the study of crack initiation and propagation in a wide range of problems, including the onset and propagation in the neighbourhood of a crack tip, as well as the onset of a debond in the absence of a crack tip.
